recipe.goal: Extract spectra and continuum fluxes and measure line parameters
recipe.method: Convolve all images to a common 0.54'' circular beam, extract spectra and continuum flux from a 0.50'' diameter circular aperture centered on the HC1 continuum peak, identify lines using CDMS and JPL databases, and fit Gaussian profiles (or directly integrate) to measure line parameters
key_parameters: Aperture diameter = 0.50'' (560 au); convolved circular beam = 0.54''
Detection threshold = 3 sigma at V_sys = -8.0 km s^-1 (tentative = 2.5 to 3 sigma); upper limit assumed FWHM = 4 km s^-1 at 2 sigma

recipe.goal: Construct integrated intensity maps and measure deconvolved source sizes
recipe.method: Integrate spectral cubes over velocity ranges of detected emission (stacking multiple lines for some species) and fit 2D Gaussian profiles to estimate deconvolved source sizes
key_parameters: Upper limit set when deconvolved size is smaller than half the beam size

recipe.goal: Derive molecular rotational temperatures and column densities
recipe.method: Perform rotation diagram analysis under LTE and optically thin assumptions for species with multiple transitions; assume T_rot for species with single/few transitions; scale from rare isotopologues for optically thick or undetected main species; also report non-LTE column densities for selected species in Table 3
key_parameters: Assumed T_rot = 20-40 K for extended species (H13CO+, HC18O+, CCH, CN, H13CN, HC15N, c-C3H2); T_rot = 50-150 K for SiO, H2CO, HDCO, D2CO
assumptions: LTE and optically thin conditions; 12C/13C = 66 and 32S/34S = 22 with 30% uncertainty; ortho/para ratio of 3 for c-C3H2, H2CO, H2CS; E/A ratio of 1 for CH3OH

recipe.goal: Derive H2 column densities, gas number densities, hot gas mass, and molecular fractional abundances
recipe.method: Calculate N(H2) from 1.2 mm and 0.87 mm dust continuum brightness assuming optically thin dust emission, average the two bands for HC1, and divide N(X) by N(H2) to obtain fractional abundances
key_parameters: T_d = 100-150 K; kappa_1.2mm = 2.27 cm^2 g^-1; kappa_0.87mm = 3.53 cm^2 g^-1; dust-to-gas ratio Z = 0.008; source size = 600 au
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission; bare dust grain opacity from (cite: Oss94); dust-to-gas mass ratio Z = 0.008; T_d = 100-150 K

recipe.method: Compile 3 to 500 um photometric data from 2MASS, AllWISE, and Herschel Hi-GAL via IRSA and estimate bolometric luminosities of HC1 and HC2
assumptions: Point-source far-infrared fluxes at HC1 and HC2 positions dominate their bolometric luminosities

recipe.goal: Simulate gas-phase COM lifetimes under enhanced cosmic-ray/X-ray ionization
recipe.method: Numerically solve pseudo-time-dependent gas-phase chemical network models using the Rokko code for varying ionization rates
key_parameters: n(H2) = 10^7 cm^-3; T_gas = 150 K; A_V = 20 mag; ionization rate zeta = 10^-17 to 10^-14 s^-1
assumptions: Fixed physical conditions (n_H2 = 10^7 cm^-3, T = 150 K, A_V = 20 mag); X-ray and cosmic-ray ionization not distinguished; initial abundances from typical interstellar ices and HC1 COMs (Table 11)
